q: The state of Andhra Pradesh gets its most of the rain fall during
explanation:
Most books and keys: August–September. Strictly: by IMD 1989–2018 means the three months June–August hold more rain (366 mm) than August–September (289 mm), though August (143 mm) and September (146 mm) are the two wettest single months; NextGen/Rocket name July as the rainiest month (IMD rainfall monograph 2020 p.5; NextGen AP Geography 02 p.6).
AP gets about two-thirds of its rain from the SW monsoon (mid-June–September), and by IMD state means August and September are its two wettest months, so the key is August–September. November–December (NE monsoon) matters mainly for Nellore and Rayalaseema; January–February is the dry winter.

notes.text: - **"Most of AP's rain falls in August–September"** – the exam key; by IMD means August and September are the two wettest months.

exam: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
q: Sri. Venkateswara National Park is famous for the protection of the:
explanation:
App's earlier key: spotted deer. Strictly: spotted deer live in the park, but the golden gecko is its flagship/indicator species (en.wikipedia.org Sri Venkateswara National Park; AP Forest Department indicator list, via web search).
Sri Venkateswara NP's indicator species is the golden gecko (with the slender loris, red sanders and Cycas beddomei); the spotted deer is a common ungulate found in most AP forests, and the bullfrog and black-naped hare are not its flagship species.
